thread:
incident-bot: PAGER — multiple 502/504s reported from CascadeClient (private VPC) for /v1/infer and /healthcheck from 6765432030–6765432090. Source: priv-edge-nlb-us-west-2.

mira: saw the alert, paging on-call. suspect healthcheck failures at the ALB -> target group.

arnold: I'm oncall, looking. can someone drop the last few logs?

devops-bot: Recent deploy note: cascade-client pushed a security group change 12:03 UTC that tightened inbound rules on the worker subnet (sg-0a1b2c3d).

arnold: thx. mira, can you confirm if NLB health probes are reaching the ALB?

mira: running curl from priv-edge host to internal ALB IP now: `curl -sv http://10.2.14.22:8080/health` -> connection reset. tcpdump shows RSTs from instance IPs.

arnold: that smells like SG or host firewall blocking the healthcheck source CIDR. cascade-noc, can you confirm any recent ACL/SG changes on your side?

cascade-noc: we applied a tightened SG rule as part of a compliance sprint ~12:00UTC, allowed only 10.0.0.0/16. We didn't include Redwood probe ranges. We saw brief errors and opened this thread.

arnold: ok — root cause likely SG blocked priv-edge health probes (Redwood edge IPs). mitigation options: 1) cascade grants temporary allow for Redwood probe CIDR 52.65.128.0/24, 2) change ALB healthcheck to use an internal path that bypasses the restricted rule (not ideal), 3) route traffic via dedicated pool. What's fastest?

cascade-noc: we can add an allow rule quickly. adding inbound allow TCP 8080 from 52.65.128.0/24 now.

mira: rechecking health from priv-edge host... healthcheck now succeeds 200 OK, backend transitions healthy in TG. Errors dropping. :white_check_mark:

arnold: great. keep the allow rule for 1 hour while we monitor, then we'll coordinate a tighter CIDR or tag-based SG with you for long-term.

shelly: logging note — I increased alert sensitivity on the /healthcheck 502 spike and created a temporary dashboard panel to show healthcheck success rate by AZ.

cascade-noc: monitoring shows traffic normalized across targets. We'll schedule a change window to add explicit Redwood probe tags and update our IaC to prevent regressions.

arnold: follow-ups: 1) add runbook step for privnet customers to whitelist Redwood probe CIDRs before SG changes (mira + shelly), 2) schedule meeting with CascadeClient NOC to add tag-based SG rule (arnold + cascade-noc), 3) add alert that detects sudden SG rule removals affecting healthchecks (shelly).

mira: documenting incident in ops board, tagging customer ID CAS-4721. closing paging for now, will reopen if error rate >1% for 10m. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (temporary mitigation applied). Record: 6765432100.
